key_insight: Task-specific OCT scan quality gating works better with learned image representations than with standard scalar NR-IQA metrics, especially for choroid segmentation.
clinical_relevance: Better quality gating could reduce failed or unreliable automated retinal segmentations, improving the robustness of OCT-based biomarker pipelines in real-world settings.
method: Compared scalar NR-IQA metrics with pretrained embeddings as quality gates for OCT B-scans.
Evaluated supervised linear probing and unsupervised K-Means clustering on feature vectors.
Tested general-purpose ImageNet models and retinal foundation models, including RETFound.
evidence_signal: The study analyzed 6,076 OCT B-scans from 80 subjects and found scalar metrics were weak (|r| < 0.20), while pretrained representations improved ROC-AUC up to 0.81.
watch_item: Performance was assessed for a specific task and dataset, so quality-gate behavior may vary across scanners, diseases, and segmentation models.
paper_title: Task-Specific Quality Gating for Retinal Optical Coherence Tomography B-Scans: Learned Representations Over Scalar Metrics in Choroid Segmentation
